newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hopewell up on laggard hunting.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell up on laggard hunting.

text.p: Shares of Hopewell Holdings Ltd rose on Wednesday on demand for laggards after the recent rally in blue-chip and red-chip stocks, brokers said.
Brokers said rumours of a covered warrant issue on the stock following expiry of some existing warrants also underpinned buying.
Hopewell shares rose HK$0.20 to HK$4.70 just before the midday break after touching a high of HK$4.75.
Volume was 51.24 million shares worth HK$239.37 million.
"Investors switched to laggards, such as Hopewell, following the recent rally in blue chips and red chips," said Sean Li, associate director of Amsteel Securities.
"(Hopewell's) financial burden is seen released after its sales of CEPA, and that also support buying," Li said.
"The CEPA sale was finalised a month ago and there has been a pick-up in buying since then," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading at HG Asia.

In January, Southern Co completed the purchase of an 80 percent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) from Hopewell and other CEPA shareholders. The deal has generated cash proceeds of HK$10.8 billion for Hopewell.
